claims.claim: Node can handle 50,000 open WebSockets and realtime matchmaking for launch
claims.why: The benchmarks only cover short HTTP requests on up to 256 connections, with no long-lived WebSocket or 50k-connection test.

claims.claim: Run 6–10 pods, each holding roughly 5–10k sockets; idle sockets are cheap, memory is mostly per-connection buffers
claims.why: No test measured sockets per process or memory per idle connection; peak memory was only recorded at 64–256 connections.

claims.claim: Elixir/BEAM (Phoenix Channels) is the best technical fit, with lightweight processes, proven at this scale
claims.measured: I/O wait at 256 connections: 18,711 req/s at 160 MB, vs node-fastify at 17,462 req/s and 69 MB
claims.why: The benchmarks don't test Phoenix Channels, presence, or anything near tens of thousands of concurrent connections, so they can't confirm 'proven at this scale'.

claims.claim: Go is solid for this, with good concurrency and low memory use
claims.measured: Peak memory 7–16 MB vs 55–77 MB for node-express and node-fastify; I/O wait 20,235 (gin) and 18,905 (net/http) req/s vs node-fastify at 17,462
claims.why: Go used far less memory than Node in every test and handled concurrent I/O-wait load slightly better than Node.
